summary: Gated. Anyone can create a LinkedIn app and get sign-in (profile, email) plus posting as the member (w_member_social) self-serve. Company pages, analytics, ads and sales data need LinkedIn's approval. That is only open to registered legal organizations, goes through a development tier then a standard tier, and a rejection means starting again with a new app. Decide which product you actually need before you build.

oauth_support_claim.text: LinkedIn uses OAuth 2.0 and publishes an OpenID Connect discovery document.

difficulty_claim.text: Only 'Open Permissions' (sign-in and member posting) are self-serve. Most other permissions and partner programs need explicit approval from LinkedIn.
difficulty_claim.quote: Most permissions and partner programs require explicit approval from LinkedIn.

claim.text: Not confirmed whether Composio manages a LinkedIn OAuth app. Even a managed app cannot give you scopes LinkedIn has not approved for that app.
claim.note: Set COMPOSIO_API_KEY and regenerate to check the live catalog.

endpoints.note: Read from LinkedIn's live OpenID discovery document on 2026-10-28.

hands_on.text: 15-30 minutes for a self-serve app; days of prep for a partner application

approval_wait.text: Self-serve products: none. Partner products: not published. LinkedIn says it may contact you up to 60 days after some access forms.
approval_wait.quote: LinkedIn will contact you up to 60 days after the form submission only if we will identify meeting access criteria and a strong partnership fit.
approval_wait.note: From LinkedIn's 'Increasing Access' page (search snippet). It applies to Marketing access increases, not to every program.

fastest_path.text: Use 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn' right away. Apply for Community Management API development tier in parallel if you need company pages.

steps.title: Create the app and associate a LinkedIn Page
steps.detail: Each app must be tied to a company Page. A super admin of that Page has to verify the app. If you administer the Page, this is quick.
steps.why_human: LinkedIn login and Page admin approval.
steps.quote: Ensure a super admin of the LinkedIn Page associated with your organization has verified your application.
steps.note: The source states this for gated (Community Management) access. That the app creation form itself requires a Page comes from developer reports and was not verified against official docs.

steps.title: Do not use 'Linked' or 'In' in the app name or logo
steps.detail: Apps that include LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos are rejected in vetting.
steps.quote: Ensure that your application doesn't include any portion of the LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos

steps.title: Add self-serve products
steps.detail: Products tab: 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' (openid, profile, email) and 'Share on LinkedIn' (w_member_social).
steps.quote: Open Permissions are the only permissions that are available to all developers without special approval.

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URL and copy credentials
steps.detail: Auth tab: add the redirect URL from your Composio auth config, then copy the client ID and secret.

phases.name: Apply for gated access (if needed)
phases.summary: Company pages, analytics, ads, sales or talent data.

steps.title: Check your use case is allowed
steps.detail: Read the API terms and the restricted-use list. Community Management is commercial-only, for registered legal organizations.
steps.quote: our Community Management APIs are only available to registered legal organizations for commercial use cases only

steps.title: Submit the development tier access form
steps.detail: Needs a verified business email (personal email fails), legal name, registered address, website and privacy policy.
steps.why_human: Business identity documents and email verification.
steps.quote: Personal email addresses won't pass the vetting process.

steps.title: Build the integration, then apply for standard tier with a screencast
steps.detail: Record a narrated, downloadable, high-resolution screencast of each use case, and provide test credentials.
steps.quote: Ensure the screen recording is high resolution and downloadable.

requirements.title: LinkedIn company Page with a super admin
Registered legal organization (gated products)
requirements.detail: Individuals and personal emails do not pass vetting for Community Management.

gotchas.title: No refresh tokens for most apps
gotchas.detail: Access tokens last 60 days. Programmatic refresh tokens (365 days, not extended by refreshing) are only for approved Marketing Developer Platform partners. Self-serve apps must send users through OAuth again.
gotchas.quote: LinkedIn supports programmatic refresh tokens for all approved Marketing Developer Platform (MDP) partners.

gotchas.title: A rejection means a new app
gotchas.detail: If a development or standard tier request is rejected, you cannot reapply with the same app. You have to create a new app and start again.
gotchas.quote: You won't be able to re-apply for Development tier access with your existing app.

gotchas.title: Compliance APIs are closed
gotchas.detail: r_compliance and w_compliance cannot be requested.
gotchas.quote: Access is closed and may not be requested.

blockers.title: Partner approval for company pages, ads, sales and talent data
blockers.detail: LinkedIn decides. Approval is not guaranteed and can be revoked later for non-compliance.
blockers.workaround: Limit v1 to member sign-in and member posting. Apply for development tier early, with a business email and a verified Page.

blockers.title: Reading other members' data or messaging at scale
blockers.detail: No self-serve product offers this, and the partner programs cover specific use cases.
blockers.workaround: Redesign the feature around the member's own content, or apply to the matching partner program.
blockers.note: Inferred from the permission list. LinkedIn does not state it in one sentence.

audit.method: Fetched 'Getting Access' and 'Community Management App Review' on 2026-10-28.
audit.note: Sharpened: sign-in and member posting are self-serve. Company pages and other products are gated and need a legal entity.
Refresh tokens are only for approved MDP partners. Self-serve apps get 60-day access tokens and users have to re-consent.

audit.claim: Partner review takes up to 60 days
audit.note: That page covers Marketing access increases. No published time for Community Management tiers.
The discovery document does not advertise PKCE methods. That is recorded as observed, not as 'PKCE unsupported'.
